outcome: breastfeeding initiation within the first hours of life
cohort: The study included HTLV-1-infected (n=17) and uninfected (n=34) pregnant women admitted for delivery at a university maternity hospital in Salvador, Brazil between 2020 and 2022.
finding: HTLV-1-positive women had higher rates of unplanned and undesired pregnancies, metabolic disorders, hypertension/eclampsia, and lower rates of breastfeeding initiation within the first hours of life compared to uninfected women.
